items.title: Bound the copy-induced blind spot of `resolved`
items.state: Ruled; the guard lives in the precedence and witness cases.
items.detail: `attributeDeparture` returns `resolved` for any matching rule in the `bootstrap` layer, including curated, scoped, and restore copies. The preservation gate therefore cannot see a departure that a copy introduces. The audit held this. The Orchestrator bounded it with the precedence case, which proves no copy gains a precedence its original lacks, and with the per-row witnesses. The preservation brief also relies on probe-4's one-time copy-induced check, which no run repeated after the token map.
items.proposed_disposition: Record this as a later item. In the next unit that touches the preservation reader, split copies out of `resolved` into a `curated` cause, with a planted copy that departs on a non-witness element as the control.
items.verify_reason:
This item is still open. Nothing closes it: the split has not landed, and no record files it as a later item. The trigger in the proposed disposition has already fired once without the split. T3 rewrote the preservation reader and left copies in `resolved`.

The token round also weakened the guard that the ruling relies on:
- The witness case and the preservation gate both read the tuned sheet alone. That sheet carries every copy.
- As a result, the witness case no longer compares a hazard element against Bootstrap alone. A copy that outranks `.table-primary` or `.table-group-divider` reads the same value in both frames.
- The precedence case is the only remaining guard against a copy that gains precedence.
- A copy can also depart through inheritance, where it restores `inherit` but its parent lacks a copy. The gate still sees that kind of departure, and it still lands in `resolved`. The gate read 75 such departures at 1280 px and 28 at 390 px after the map.
- Probe-4's copy check is the only run that separated copy-induced departures from `resolved`. It ran once, before the token map, and recorded 1,960 hits. Every hit is a border color on a `:where(.table) th`, `:where(.table) td`, or `:where(.table-group-divider) td` copy. Fold-2 kept the `:where(.table) tr` and `tfoot` rows that the probe did not reproduce, but no record rules the hits by name.

Recommendation: run this before stage B as part of the Tailwind completion checklist, not as a later item, because the user's word of 2026-10-05 puts the whole track before stage B. Do not put it in the journey-tuning unit: that unit's rows gate requires the resolved-value readings to stay unchanged.

The unit has three parts:
1. Split copies out of `resolved` into a `curated` cause in `attributeDeparture`. For the control, plant a copy that is present only in the recipe and departs on an element that is not a witness.
2. Re-run the copy check against the mapped tuned sheet.
